vs-a1-first-day.objectives.0.textTr: Tell Sofia your name, where you are from and what you do, using am / is / are.
vs-a1-first-day.objectives.1.textTr: Ask Sofia where she is from and what her job is.

vs-a1-gift-shop.objectives.0.textTr: Ask what things are using this, that, these and those (What's this? What are those?).
vs-a1-gift-shop.objectives.1.textTr: Choose a present and say what you want with a / an and plurals (I'd like a mug and two postcards).

vs-a1-lost-property.objectives.0.textTr: Say what you lost and describe it with my (It's my blue bag).
vs-a1-lost-property.objectives.1.textTr: Answer Tom's questions about which things are yours (Is this your phone?).

vs-a1-hotel-desk.objectives.0.textTr: Ask three questions about the hotel with Is / Are / Where / What (Where is the breakfast room? Is the wifi free?).
vs-a1-hotel-desk.objectives.1.textTr: Answer Maria's questions about you (Are you here for work?).

vs-a1-neighbour-chat.objectives.0.textTr: Tell Ben about your day: what time you get up, where you work or study, when you go to bed (I get up at seven).
vs-a1-neighbour-chat.objectives.1.textTr: Ask Ben about his day with Do you…? and What time do you…?
vs-a1-neighbour-chat.keyPhrases.2.tr: What time do you start work?

vs-a1-gym-signup.objectives.0.textTr: Tell Mia how often you do things using always, usually, often, sometimes, never (I sometimes swim).
vs-a1-gym-signup.objectives.1.textTr: Ask Mia how often she trains or does something (How often do you…?).
vs-a1-gym-signup.keyPhrases.0.tr: I usually walk in the evening.

vs-a1-city-directions.objectives.0.textTr: Ask if there is a place near here (Is there a pharmacy near here? Are there any banks?).
vs-a1-city-directions.objectives.1.textTr: Repeat the directions back to check (It's next to the bookshop, right?).
vs-a1-city-directions.keyPhrases.0.tr: Is there a pharmacy near here?

vs-a1-party-hobbies.aiRole: Someone you meet at the party
vs-a1-party-hobbies.objectives.0.textTr: Tell Chloe two things you like or love doing and one you hate (I love cooking. I hate waiting).
vs-a1-party-hobbies.objectives.1.textTr: Ask Chloe what she enjoys doing (What do you enjoy doing?).

vs-a1-phone-call.titleTr: A Phone Call with a Friend
vs-a1-phone-call.objectives.0.textTr: Say what you are doing right now and what is happening around you (I'm cooking. My brother is watching TV).
vs-a1-phone-call.objectives.1.textTr: Ask Leo what he is doing and suggest meeting later.

vs-a1-flatshare.objectives.0.textTr: Say two things you can do and one thing you can't (I can cook, but I can't drive).
vs-a1-flatshare.objectives.1.textTr: Ask politely for two things with Can I…? or Could you…? (Can I use the kitchen?).

vs-a1-grocery.objectives.0.textTr: Ask for things you need with some and any (I need some tomatoes. Do you have any eggs?).
vs-a1-grocery.objectives.1.textTr: Ask about price and quantity (How much is it? How many do I need?).

vs-a1-where-were-you.objectives.0.textTr: Say where you were yesterday and how it was (I was at the cinema. It was great).
vs-a1-where-were-you.objectives.1.textTr: Ask Emma where she was and who was with her (Where were you? Were you alone?).

vs-a1-weekend-chat.objectives.0.textTr: Tell Jack what you did at the weekend with at least three past verbs (I visited…, I went…, I saw…).
vs-a1-weekend-chat.objectives.1.textTr: Ask Jack two questions with did (Did you…?).

vs-a2-weekend-trip.objectives.0.textTr: Say what you are going to do on the trip (I'm going to visit the old town).
vs-a2-weekend-trip.objectives.1.textTr: Agree on a time and a place with the present continuous (We're meeting at the station at ten).
vs-a2-weekend-trip.keyPhrases.0.tr: I'm going to take lots of photos.
vs-a2-weekend-trip.keyPhrases.2.tr: What are you going to do there?

vs-a2-helping-move.objectives.0.textTr: Offer to help with two things using I'll… (I'll carry the boxes).
vs-a2-helping-move.objectives.1.textTr: Make a promise and a prediction (I'll be there at nine. It won't take long).
vs-a2-helping-move.keyPhrases.0.tr: I'll help you with the boxes.
vs-a2-helping-move.keyPhrases.1.tr: Don't worry, I'll be there at nine.
vs-a2-helping-move.keyPhrases.2.tr: I think it will be easy.

vs-a2-phone-shop.objectives.0.textTr: Compare the two phones with comparatives (The Titan is faster than the Nova).
vs-a2-phone-shop.objectives.1.textTr: Choose one phone and say why, with a superlative or as … as (It's the best for me).
vs-a2-phone-shop.keyPhrases.1.tr: This one is better than that one.

vs-a2-doctor-visit.objectives.0.textTr: Describe your problem and ask for advice (What should I do?).
vs-a2-doctor-visit.objectives.1.textTr: Say what you have to do this week and ask what you must or mustn't do (I have to work on Friday).
vs-a2-doctor-visit.keyPhrases.0.tr: I have a headache and a sore throat.

vs-a2-have-you-ever.objectives.0.textTr: Ask Tara two 'Have you ever…?' questions.
vs-a2-have-you-ever.objectives.1.textTr: Tell Tara things you have done and never done (I've been to Italy. I've never tried sushi).
vs-a2-have-you-ever.keyPhrases.0.tr: Have you ever been to Japan?
vs-a2-have-you-ever.keyPhrases.2.tr: I've already seen the old town.

vs-a2-who-ate-the-cake.objectives.0.textTr: Say what you were doing yesterday at 3 pm and at 5 pm (I was reading at three).
vs-a2-who-ate-the-cake.objectives.1.textTr: Use when and while to tell your story (I was cooking while my brother was watching TV).
vs-a2-who-ate-the-cake.keyPhrases.1.tr: I was cooking when you called.

vs-a2-driving-lesson.objectives.0.textTr: Say how you do things with adverbs (I drive carefully. I speak slowly).
vs-a2-driving-lesson.objectives.1.textTr: Ask for feedback and answer (Did I drive well?).

vs-a2-party-plan.objectives.0.textTr: Say what you have and what you need with a lot of, a few and a little (We have a lot of snacks. We need a few chairs).
vs-a2-party-plan.objectives.1.textTr: Point out a problem with too much / too many (There are too many balloons).
vs-a2-party-plan.keyPhrases.0.tr: We need a few more chairs.
vs-a2-party-plan.keyPhrases.2.tr: We have a lot of snacks.

vs-a2-picnic-plans.objectives.0.textTr: Make plans for different weather with if (If it rains, we'll go to the museum).
vs-a2-picnic-plans.objectives.1.textTr: Ask and answer 'What will you do if…?' and say a general truth (If I'm tired, I stay at home).
vs-a2-picnic-plans.keyPhrases.0.tr: If it rains, we'll stay home.
vs-a2-picnic-plans.keyPhrases.1.tr: What will you do if it's cold?

vs-a2-why-late.objectives.0.textTr: Tell what happened in order with first, then, after that and finally.
vs-a2-why-late.objectives.1.textTr: Explain reasons and results with because, so and but (I missed the bus, so I walked).
vs-a2-why-late.keyPhrases.1.tr: Then I walked, but it was far.
vs-a2-why-late.keyPhrases.2.tr: I'm late because there was traffic.

vs-b1-job-interview.objectives.0.textTr: Say how long you have done things using for and since (I've worked in retail since 2021).
vs-b1-job-interview.objectives.1.textTr: Answer the probing question about your short job or gap and justify it.
vs-b1-job-interview.objectives.2.textTr: Ask two good questions about the team or the job at the end.
vs-b1-job-interview.keyPhrases.0.tr: I've worked as a designer for three years.
vs-b1-job-interview.keyPhrases.1.tr: I've lived in this city since 2019.
vs-b1-job-interview.keyPhrases.2.tr: How long has the team been together?

vs-b1-catching-up.objectives.0.textTr: Describe what you have been doing lately with the present perfect continuous (I've been studying a lot).
vs-b1-catching-up.objectives.1.textTr: Explain how you feel because of it (I've been working late, so I'm exhausted).
vs-b1-catching-up.objectives.2.textTr: Respond to Daniel's request for a place to stay: decide and give your reasons.
vs-b1-catching-up.keyPhrases.0.tr: I've been working a lot lately.
vs-b1-catching-up.keyPhrases.1.tr: I've been trying to learn the guitar.
vs-b1-catching-up.keyPhrases.2.tr: How long have you been living there?

vs-b1-old-neighbourhood.objectives.0.textTr: Describe how things used to be (There used to be a cinema here).
vs-b1-old-neighbourhood.objectives.1.textTr: Talk about childhood habits with used to and would (We would play outside until dark).
vs-b1-old-neighbourhood.objectives.2.textTr: Compare then and now and say whether the change is good, with a reason.
vs-b1-old-neighbourhood.keyPhrases.0.tr: We used to play football in the street.
vs-b1-old-neighbourhood.keyPhrases.1.tr: There didn't use to be so much traffic.
vs-b1-old-neighbourhood.keyPhrases.2.tr: Every summer we would go to the lake.

vs-b1-missed-flight.objectives.0.textTr: Explain what had already happened before you arrived (When I got there, the gate had closed).
vs-b1-missed-flight.objectives.1.textTr: Give the reasons in order, mixing the past perfect and the past simple.
vs-b1-missed-flight.objectives.2.textTr: Negotiate a solution: ask for the best option and decide.
vs-b1-missed-flight.keyPhrases.0.tr: By the time I got there, the gate had closed.
vs-b1-missed-flight.keyPhrases.1.tr: I had left on time, but the bus had broken down.
vs-b1-missed-flight.keyPhrases.2.tr: Is there any way to change my ticket for free?

vs-b1-radio-phone-in.objectives.0.textTr: Answer two 'What would you do if…?' questions with the full second conditional.
vs-b1-radio-phone-in.objectives.1.textTr: Ask Jamie a hypothetical question of your own (If you could…, what would you…?).
vs-b1-radio-phone-in.objectives.2.textTr: Defend one of your answers when Jamie challenges it.
vs-b1-radio-phone-in.keyPhrases.0.tr: If I won the lottery, I would travel the world.
vs-b1-radio-phone-in.keyPhrases.1.tr: If I were the mayor, I'd build more parks.
vs-b1-radio-phone-in.keyPhrases.2.tr: What would you do if you were me?

vs-b1-mystery-bag.objectives.0.textTr: Make deductions with must, might, could and can't (It must be Mike's; it can't be Marta's).
vs-b1-mystery-bag.objectives.1.textTr: Ask Alex questions to get more clues.
vs-b1-mystery-bag.objectives.2.textTr: Agree on what to do with the bag and why.
vs-b1-mystery-bag.keyPhrases.1.tr: It can't be Marta's. She's on holiday.
vs-b1-mystery-bag.keyPhrases.2.tr: It might belong to a visitor.

vs-b1-hardware-store.objectives.0.textTr: Ask for three things by describing them (It's something that you use to hang pictures).
vs-b1-hardware-store.objectives.1.textTr: Describe a place or a person with who or where (It's a shop where you can…).
vs-b1-hardware-store.objectives.2.textTr: Check you have the right item and explain what you will use it for.
vs-b1-hardware-store.keyPhrases.0.tr: It's a thing that you use to hang pictures.
vs-b1-hardware-store.keyPhrases.1.tr: I'm looking for a tool which cuts metal.
vs-b1-hardware-store.keyPhrases.2.tr: Do you mean the one that has a long handle?

vs-b1-factory-tour.objectives.0.textTr: Ask three questions with the passive (How is it made? When was it built?).
vs-b1-factory-tour.objectives.1.textTr: Explain how a traditional food or product from your country is made, using the passive (First the dough is rolled).
vs-b1-factory-tour.objectives.2.textTr: Sum up what you learned in two or three sentences (It is exported to forty countries).
vs-b1-factory-tour.keyPhrases.2.tr: First the dough is rolled out.

vs-b1-what-did-she-say.objectives.0.textTr: Report what your manager said and asked (She said that…, She asked me if…).
vs-b1-what-did-she-say.objectives.1.textTr: Report what she told you to do (She told me to…, She asked me not to…).
vs-b1-what-did-she-say.objectives.2.textTr: Report your own answer and how it ended (I told her that…).
vs-b1-what-did-she-say.keyPhrases.0.tr: She said that the project was finished.
vs-b1-what-did-she-say.keyPhrases.1.tr: He asked me if I could stay late.
vs-b1-what-did-she-say.keyPhrases.2.tr: She told me to call the client.

vs-b1-tourist-office.objectives.0.textTr: Ask three polite indirect questions (Could you tell me…? Do you know if…?).
vs-b1-tourist-office.objectives.1.textTr: Check information with question tags (The museum opens at nine, doesn't it?).
vs-b1-tourist-office.objectives.2.textTr: Plan a half-day programme with Hugo and confirm the final plan.
vs-b1-tourist-office.keyPhrases.0.tr: Could you tell me where the museum is?
vs-b1-tourist-office.keyPhrases.1.tr: Do you know what time it closes?

vs-b1-habit-coach.objectives.0.textTr: Talk about habits you want to start or stop with verb + -ing / to (I want to start running; I should give up eating late).
vs-b1-habit-coach.objectives.1.textTr: Use remember, stop or try with a clear difference in meaning (I stopped to drink water / I stopped drinking coffee).
vs-b1-habit-coach.objectives.2.textTr: Make a three-step plan and promise it to Dana.
vs-b1-habit-coach.keyPhrases.0.tr: I'd like to give up eating sweets.
vs-b1-habit-coach.keyPhrases.2.tr: I always forget to drink water.

vs-b2-no-regrets.objectives.0.textTr: Talk about a past regret with the third conditional (If I had studied harder, I would have passed).
vs-b2-no-regrets.objectives.1.textTr: Link a past decision with your life today, using a mixed conditional (If I had moved, I'd be living there now).
vs-b2-no-regrets.objectives.2.textTr: Advise Leila on her decision using what you learned from your own choices.
vs-b2-no-regrets.keyPhrases.0.tr: If I had known, I would have acted differently.
vs-b2-no-regrets.keyPhrases.1.tr: If I hadn't moved, I wouldn't have met my partner.
vs-b2-no-regrets.keyPhrases.2.tr: If I were you, I wouldn't hesitate.

vs-b2-post-mortem.objectives.0.textTr: Speculate about causes (The email might have gone to spam; he can't have received it).
vs-b2-post-mortem.objectives.1.textTr: Say what should or shouldn't have been done (We should have confirmed the date).
vs-b2-post-mortem.objectives.2.textTr: Agree on two lessons learned with Olivia.
vs-b2-post-mortem.keyPhrases.0.tr: He must have forgotten to call.
vs-b2-post-mortem.keyPhrases.1.tr: We should have checked the date.
vs-b2-post-mortem.keyPhrases.2.tr: It can't have been her fault.

vs-b2-handover.objectives.0.textTr: Say what you will be doing at key moments (On Monday morning I'll be sitting in a meeting).
vs-b2-handover.objectives.1.textTr: Say what will have been finished by each deadline (By Friday I'll have sent the report).
vs-b2-handover.objectives.2.textTr: Negotiate Marcus's request for an earlier file and agree a deal.
vs-b2-handover.keyPhrases.0.tr: This time next week I'll be flying to Tokyo.
vs-b2-handover.keyPhrases.1.tr: By Friday, I'll have finished the report.
vs-b2-handover.keyPhrases.2.tr: Will you be available on Thursday?

vs-b2-renovation-quote.objectives.0.textTr: Say what you want to have done (I'd like to have the kitchen painted).
vs-b2-renovation-quote.objectives.1.textTr: Ask about time and cost (How long will it take to get the windows replaced?).
vs-b2-renovation-quote.objectives.2.textTr: Decide what to do yourself and what to have done before the party, and agree the deal.
vs-b2-renovation-quote.keyPhrases.0.tr: I'd like to have the walls painted.
vs-b2-renovation-quote.keyPhrases.1.tr: How much would it cost to get the roof repaired?
vs-b2-renovation-quote.keyPhrases.2.tr: I'll paint it myself, but I'll have the windows fixed.

vs-b2-witness-at-work.objectives.0.textTr: Report what colleagues said with reporting verbs (He admitted breaking it; she denied taking the file).
vs-b2-witness-at-work.objectives.1.textTr: Stay precise about what you heard and what you assume (I'm not sure whether…, as far as I know).
vs-b2-witness-at-work.objectives.2.textTr: Suggest a fair solution (I suggest talking to them together).
vs-b2-witness-at-work.keyPhrases.2.tr: I suggest talking to them together.

vs-b2-introducing-guests.objectives.0.textTr: Introduce three people with extra information in non-defining clauses (This is Marta, who works at a hospital).
vs-b2-introducing-guests.objectives.1.textTr: Describe a place or an event with which or where (We met in Lisbon, which is my favourite city).
vs-b2-introducing-guests.objectives.2.textTr: Add one surprising fact about a guest with whose (Jonas, whose band is famous, will play later).
vs-b2-introducing-guests.keyPhrases.0.tr: This is Marta, who I've known for ten years.
vs-b2-introducing-guests.keyPhrases.1.tr: We stayed in Lisbon, which was amazing.
vs-b2-introducing-guests.keyPhrases.2.tr: Her brother, whose band is famous, will play later.

vs-b2-two-offers.objectives.0.textTr: Compare the two offers with whereas and while (Job A is stable, whereas Job B is risky).
vs-b2-two-offers.objectives.1.textTr: Concede a point and still argue your case with although, despite or in spite of (Although it pays less, I'd choose it).
vs-b2-two-offers.objectives.2.textTr: Defend your final decision when Rosa pushes back.
vs-b2-two-offers.keyPhrases.0.tr: Although it pays less, it's more flexible.
vs-b2-two-offers.keyPhrases.1.tr: Despite the long commute, I'd take it.
vs-b2-two-offers.keyPhrases.2.tr: Job A is stable, whereas Job B is risky.

vs-b2-hotel-manager.objectives.0.textTr: Make a strong complaint using at least two inversions (Never have I stayed in such a dirty room; Not only was it noisy, but…).
vs-b2-hotel-manager.objectives.1.textTr: Refuse weak apologies firmly but politely (Under no circumstances will I accept that).
vs-b2-hotel-manager.objectives.2.textTr: Negotiate fair compensation and agree what happens next.
vs-b2-hotel-manager.keyPhrases.0.tr: Never have I seen such a mess.
vs-b2-hotel-manager.keyPhrases.1.tr: Not only was the room noisy, but it was also dirty.
vs-b2-hotel-manager.keyPhrases.2.tr: Under no circumstances will I pay for this.

vs-c1-investor-pitch.objectives.0.textTr: Stress your key points with what-clefts (What sets us apart is our support).
vs-c1-investor-pitch.objectives.1.textTr: Correct Victoria's misunderstanding with an it-cleft (It wasn't the price; it was the delivery that put people off).
vs-c1-investor-pitch.objectives.2.textTr: Close by asking for a concrete next step and answering her final challenge.
vs-c1-investor-pitch.keyPhrases.0.tr: What we need is a bigger market.
vs-c1-investor-pitch.keyPhrases.1.tr: It was the timing that caused the problem.
vs-c1-investor-pitch.keyPhrases.2.tr: What sets us apart is the support we offer.

vs-c1-science-interview.objectives.0.textTr: Answer with calibrated claims (The results appear to suggest…; it tends to…; it may well be that…).
vs-c1-science-interview.objectives.1.textTr: Resist the pressure for a headline claim without losing credibility.
vs-c1-science-interview.objectives.2.textTr: Separate what the evidence shows from what is only speculation.
vs-c1-science-interview.keyPhrases.0.tr: The results appear to suggest a link.
vs-c1-science-interview.keyPhrases.1.tr: It may well be the case, but we can't be sure.
vs-c1-science-interview.keyPhrases.2.tr: That is arguably the strongest finding.

vs-c1-contract-talks.objectives.0.textTr: Make formal offers without if (Should you require changes, we would be glad to discuss them).
vs-c1-contract-talks.objectives.1.textTr: Explore concessions with hypotheticals (Were we to extend the deadline, would you accept the price?).
vs-c1-contract-talks.objectives.2.textTr: Settle the three points and express regret or responsibility diplomatically (Had we been informed earlier…).
vs-c1-contract-talks.keyPhrases.0.tr: Should you have any concerns, please let us know.
vs-c1-contract-talks.keyPhrases.1.tr: Were we to extend the deadline, would you reconsider?
vs-c1-contract-talks.keyPhrases.2.tr: Had we known earlier, we would have adjusted the plan.

vs-c1-board-report.objectives.0.textTr: Summarise results with nominalisation (The introduction of the new system led to a reduction in delays).
vs-c1-board-report.objectives.1.textTr: Explain a cause-and-effect chain concisely in a formal register.
vs-c1-board-report.objectives.2.textTr: Restate it in plain verbs when asked and say which version is clearer for this audience.
vs-c1-board-report.keyPhrases.0.tr: The introduction of the app led to an increase in sales.
vs-c1-board-report.keyPhrases.1.tr: There has been a significant decline in complaints.
vs-c1-board-report.keyPhrases.2.tr: In other words, we fixed the process and delays fell.

vs-c2-panel-debate.objectives.0.textTr: Avoid repetition with ellipsis and substitution (I think so, and so does she; I'd say they do).
vs-c2-panel-debate.objectives.1.textTr: Keep your references clear with this, such and the former / the latter.
vs-c2-panel-debate.objectives.2.textTr: Answer rapid challenges and keep the floor without being interrupted.
vs-c2-panel-debate.keyPhrases.0.tr: I'd say so, and so would most experts.
vs-c2-panel-debate.keyPhrases.1.tr: The former is cheaper; the latter is more reliable.

vs-c2-three-tones.objectives.0.textTr: Tell your friend casually, with contractions and relaxed phrasing (Hey, so my flight got cancelled).
vs-c2-three-tones.objectives.1.textTr: Tell the hotel receptionist politely and clearly, asking for what you need (I'd like to move my booking).
vs-c2-three-tones.objectives.2.textTr: Tell the conference office formally and precisely, with the exact facts (I regret to inform you that…).
vs-c2-three-tones.keyPhrases.0.tr: Hey, so my flight got cancelled.
vs-c2-three-tones.keyPhrases.1.tr: I'm afraid I won't be able to arrive until Friday.
vs-c2-three-tones.keyPhrases.2.tr: I regret to inform you that my arrival will be delayed.

vs-c2-saying-no.objectives.0.textTr: Decline clearly without a blunt no (I'm afraid that won't be possible).
vs-c2-saying-no.objectives.1.textTr: Explain your constraints and offer a real alternative (What I can offer instead is…).
vs-c2-saying-no.objectives.2.textTr: Hold your position under emotional pressure while protecting the relationship.
vs-c2-saying-no.keyPhrases.0.tr: I'm afraid that isn't something we can commit to.
vs-c2-saying-no.keyPhrases.1.tr: What I can offer instead is a phased delivery.
vs-c2-saying-no.keyPhrases.2.tr: I value our partnership, which is why I'm being honest.
